name: IRS2101STRPBF
title: 600 V high- and low-side gate driver
summary: The IRS2101 drives two N-channel MOSFETs or IGBTs: one output referred to ground and one on a floating channel, run from a bootstrap supply, that can sit up to 600 V above it. Outputs follow their inputs, which take 3.3 V, 5 V or 15 V logic; they source 130 mA and sink 270 mA at least, and the two channels' delays match within 50 ns. VCC has an undervoltage lockout. It comes in 8-lead PDIP (IRS2101PbF) and 8-lead SOIC (IRS2101SPbF, IRS2101STRPbF on tape and reel), all lead-free.

pins.name: VCC
pins.function: Supply for the input logic and the low-side output stage, 10 V to 20 V above COM; the undervoltage lockout watches it.

pins.name: HIN
pins.function: Logic command for the high-side output, referred to COM. HO is high while HIN is high.

pins.name: LIN
pins.function: Logic command for the low-side output, referred to COM. LO is high while LIN is high.

pins.name: COM
pins.function: Ground return of VCC, the logic inputs and the low-side output.

pins.name: LO
pins.function: Gate drive for the low-side switch; swings from COM to VCC.

pins.name: VS
pins.function: Floating return of the high-side channel; goes to the half-bridge midpoint, the source or emitter of the high-side switch.

pins.name: HO
pins.function: Gate drive for the high-side switch; swings from VS to VB.

pins.name: VB
pins.function: Floating supply of the high-side channel, 10 V to 20 V above VS, meant to be fed from a bootstrap capacitor.

circuits.title: Typical connection
circuits.description: One half-bridge leg of two N-channel MOSFETs driven from a single VCC rail. A capacitor across VCC and COM decouples the driver. A diode from VCC charges the capacitor between VB and VS whenever the low-side MOSFET pulls VS down; that capacitor is the floating supply for HO. Each gate is reached through a series resistor from HO or LO. The high-side drain sits on a rail of up to 600 V, decoupled to ground by its own capacitor, and the low-side source, COM and both capacitors' grounds share one ground. The high-side source (on VS) and the low-side drain each run out to the load.

parts.note: from the high-side source and VS

operation.text: Two independent gate-drive outputs for MOSFETs or IGBTs. LO is referred to COM and powered from VCC. HO is referred to VS and powered from the floating VB-VS supply, so it can drive an N-channel high-side switch whose source sits anywhere up to 600 V. The floating channel is built to run from a bootstrap supply, tolerates negative transients on VS, and is dV/dt immune; VS may slew at up to 50 V/ns.

Outputs are in phase with their inputs: HO follows HIN and LO follows LIN, and the two channels are independent. The inputs accept 3.3 V, 5 V and 15 V logic and standard CMOS or LSTTL outputs; a high is 2.5 V or more and a low 0.8 V or less over VCC = 10 V to 20 V. Each input has a Schmitt-trigger buffer and a pull-down resistor to COM.
The logic keeps working for VS from -5 V up to +600 V. When VS is between -5 V and -VBS, the output state is held.
An undervoltage detector on VCC acts on both channels. VCC rising must pass VCCUV+, 8 V to 9.8 V (8.9 V typ); VCC falling trips at VCCUV-, 7.4 V to 9 V (8.2 V typ).

The high-side command is turned into pulses, carried up to the floating channel by a high-voltage level-shift stage, cleaned by a pulse filter and stored in an RS latch, whose output drives the HO stage.

Both outputs are buffers rated for high pulse current, with little cross-conduction inside the driver. At 15 V bias a shorted output sources at least 130 mA (290 mA typ) and sinks at least 270 mA (600 mA typ) for pulses up to 10 µs. Into 1000 pF, rise time is 70 ns typ and fall time 35 ns typ.

Turn-on delay ton is from the input crossing 50 % on its rising edge to the output reaching 10 %; rise time tr is the output moving from 10 % to 90 %. Turn-off delay toff is from the input crossing 50 % on its falling edge to the output dropping to 90 %; fall time tf is the output moving from 90 % to 10 %. Delay matching MT is the gap between LO and HO crossing 10 % on turn-on, and between them crossing 90 % on turn-off.

Lead-free parts are marked S2101 on the first line, then a date code (year, work week) followed by a marking-code character, then an assembly-site character and a four-digit lot code, with a dot for pin 1. A marking-code character of P stands for a released lead-free part.
Qualified to the industrial level. The 8-lead SOIC is rated moisture sensitivity level MSL2.
